title: French Fourth Republic
capsule: The Fourth Republic was proclaimed on 27 October 1946 after a constitutional referendum and governed France during the postwar reconstruction, joining NATO (1949), co-founding the European Coal and Steel Community (1951), and losing the First Indochina War at Dien Bien Phu in May 1954. Cabinet instability was endemic — twenty-four governments in twelve years — and the Algerian War (1954–1962), begun under the republic, proved fatal. In May 1958 an army-settler uprising in Algiers threatened civil war; the National Assembly voted on 1 June 1958 to grant emergency powers to Charles de Gaulle, who oversaw the adoption of the Fifth Republic's constitution on 4 October 1958.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Metropolitan France borders are precisely known; the contested status of Algeria (legally a department, de facto a war zone from 1954) creates some ambiguity in the territorial footprint.
